function.arguments: {"finding": "The distribution of customer_segment and customer_age differs significantly between channels. The email channel has a higher proportion of loyal customers (141/359 ≈ 39.3%) compared to paid_search (29/541 ≈ 5.4%). Similarly, email has more older customers (130 out of 359 ≈ 36.2%) vs paid_search (188 out of 541 ≈ 34.8%), but the difference is smaller. The key confounder is customer_segment: loyal customers are much more likely to convert, and the email channel is heavily skewed toward them. This explains the higher conversion rate in email — it's not due to the channel itself, but because it attracts a more convert-prone segment.", "implication": "The raw comparison of conversion rates between channels is confounded by customer_segment. We cannot conclude that email is more effective unless we adjust for segment. A fair comparison requires stratification by segment or modeling the conversion rate with segment and age as covariates. Without this, the observed difference is not causal."}
function.name: note_finding
